title: How John Rush scored 1M SEO clicks: a practical checklist from domains to AI search
summary: John Rush shares his SEO playbook after 1B impressions and 1M clicks. It covers domain naming, tech basics, indexing, a weekly analytics review, low-hanging fruit in positions 8-20, human-quality blogging, backlinks via AI-cited pages, social SEO, and treating AI search as the same game.

principles.text: Push pages ranking in positions 8-20 first; they are closer to page 1 than any new article.
principles.quote: Those are closer to page 1 than any new article

principles.text: Review GSC weekly: fix high-impression, low-click queries by putting the query in H1 and meta title; update decayed pages.
principles.quote: Queries with impressions but few clicks (take the queries pointing to these pages and embed them into h1 and meta title)

principles.text: Update old pages that already get traffic before writing new ones; Google likes regular real updates.
principles.quote: Update them before writing a new one (google kinda loves to see pages being regularly updated)

principles.text: Use AI to scale blog drafts, then manually upgrade the ones gaining traction into human-quality articles with original proof.
principles.quote: Manually turn the promising ones from AI-generated into high-quality human-made articles

principles.text: Get backlinks by asking AI "best tool for X", then paying or link-swapping with authors of the cited pages.
principles.quote: Ask them to include my URL in exchange for money or a backlink from you

principles.text: Repurpose each blog post to X, LinkedIn and Reddit with a link back; social gets indexed instantly and carries weight.
principles.quote: social media backlinks in my experience have really high weight for google
